hens_rule_text: fowl allowed unless they become a habitual noise nuisance; no city hen cap confirmed, and state law protects at least 6 on single-family lots of half an acre or less
permit_notes: No city chicken permit found in official sources.
setback_notes: No city setback confirmed. State law (ARS 9-462.12) lets cities require the enclosure in the rear or side yard at least 20 feet from a neighboring property, max 200 sq ft and 8 ft high, and requires enclosures on lots under one acre to be shorter than the fence line.
coop_rules: No city coop standard confirmed; state law allows cities to require twice-weekly manure removal and rodent-proof feed storage.
zoning_notes: City Code Sec. 4-17(c) bars keeping any animal or fowl whose frequent or habitual crowing or noise disturbs a neighborhood or two or more people. Zoning district limits were not checked in the code text.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: Read the state statute ARS 9-462.12 (2024) directly; the Legislature's staff summary says Scottsdale allows fowl unless a habitual nuisance under Sec. 4-17. Scottsdale's own code and zoning text could not be opened, so any city hen cap, rooster ban or setback is unconfirmed; secondary sites claiming 5 hens and 40 ft were not trusted.
